name: Google Sheets
description: Let your AI work with Google Sheets: read any range or several at once, see a spreadsheet's tabs and sizes, append rows to a table, write and update cells and formulas, create spreadsheets and add or rename tabs. Personal Google accounts and Google Workspace.
instructions:
## Google Sheets
This connector reads and writes Google Sheets through the **Google Sheets API v4** (`https://sheets.googleapis.com/v4`): spreadsheet structure, cell values of any range, appending rows, writing and clearing ranges, creating spreadsheets and adding or renaming sheets. It works with personal Google accounts and Google Workspace, on every spreadsheet the authorizing Google account can open.

**Setup (one-time, about 10 minutes)**
1. Open https://console.cloud.google.com, pick or create a project, then **APIs & Services → Library** → enable **Google Sheets API**.
2. **APIs & Services → OAuth consent screen**: choose **Internal** if you are on Google Workspace (simplest), otherwise **External**. For External, set the publishing status to **In production**: while an app is in *Testing*, Google revokes its refresh tokens after 7 days and the connector stops working every week. For your own use, the "unverified app" warning can be clicked through.
3. **APIs & Services → Credentials → Create credentials → OAuth client ID** → application type **Web application** → add the authorized redirect URI `<your AnythingMCP URL>/api/mcp-oauth/callback` (on AnythingMCP Cloud: `https://cloud.anythingmcp.com/api/mcp-oauth/callback`).
4. Paste the client ID and secret into `GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID` and `GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET` and install the connector.
5. On the connector page, click **Authorize with Provider** and sign in with the Google account whose spreadsheets the AI should use. The refresh token is stored encrypted and access tokens are renewed automatically.

**One Google client for all Google connectors**: the same Cloud project and OAuth client can serve every Google connector (Gmail, Google Calendar, Google Drive, Google Sheets, Google Docs, Google Tasks, Search Console, Analytics, Ads). Enable each API in that project, reuse the same `GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID` and `GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET`, and authorize each connector once: each one asks only for its own scopes.

**Scope**: the connector asks for `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/spreadsheets` (read and write every spreadsheet the user can open). It does not include Google Drive, so it cannot list or search spreadsheets, move or share them. For a read-only setup, change the scope to `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/spreadsheets.readonly` in the connector's OAuth settings, authorize again, and disable `gsheets_append_rows`, `gsheets_update_range`, `gsheets_batch_update_values`, `gsheets_create_spreadsheet`, `gsheets_add_sheet` and `gsheets_rename_sheet`.

**Switched off at install**: `gsheets_clear_range` and `gsheets_batch_update` (it can delete sheets, rows and columns). Turn them on per tool if the AI needs them.

**Finding a spreadsheet**: the id is the long string in the link, `https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/<id>/edit`. To find one by name, use the Google Drive connector's `gdrive_search_files` with `mimeType = 'application/vnd.google-apps.spreadsheet' and name contains '...'`, or ask the user for the link. Then call `gsheets_get_spreadsheet` to learn the sheet names and numeric `sheetId`s.

**Ranges (A1 notation)**: `Sheet1!A1:D20`; a sheet name with spaces or symbols in single quotes, `'Sales 2026'!A:C`; whole columns `Sheet1!A:C`; open-ended `Sheet1!A2:E` (from row 2 down); a whole sheet `Sheet1`; without a sheet name the first sheet is used. Named ranges work too.

**Reading**: `gsheets_read_range` and `gsheets_batch_read` return `values` as a list of rows. Trailing empty rows and cells are omitted, so rows may have different lengths. `FORMATTED_VALUE` (default) returns what the UI shows ("1.234,50 €"); `UNFORMATTED_VALUE` returns numbers, with dates as serial numbers (days since 30 December 1899) unless `date_time_render_option` is `FORMATTED_STRING`; `FORMULA` returns the formulas. There is no pagination: read large sheets in blocks, e.g. `Data!A1:Z1000`, then `Data!A1001:Z2000`, keeping each answer small.

**Writing**
- `values` is a list of rows: `[["Date", "Amount"], ["2026-10-09", 120.5]]`. With `USER_ENTERED` (default) values are parsed as if typed: numbers, dates and formulas such as `=SUM(B2:B20)` work, using the spreadsheet's locale. `RAW` stores text exactly as given.
- `gsheets_append_rows` finds the table in `range` and adds the rows after its last row, inserting new rows so nothing below is overwritten. Use the table's columns (`Sheet1!A:E`) as range.
- `gsheets_update_range` and `gsheets_batch_update_values` overwrite the target cells. In a row, `null` leaves a cell unchanged and `""` empties it.
- `gsheets_create_spreadsheet` creates the file in the root of My Drive; `gsheets_add_sheet` adds tabs and `gsheets_rename_sheet` renames one by its numeric `sheetId`.
- `gsheets_batch_update` (switched off) accepts raw Sheets API requests for formatting, sorting, inserting or deleting rows and columns; indexes there are 0-based and end indexes exclusive.

**Limits and quotas**: a spreadsheet holds up to 10 million cells. Google allows 300 read and 300 write requests per minute per project, and 60 of each per minute per user. Over the limit it answers 429 `RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED`: wait a minute and retry, and prefer one batch call over many small ones. Keep a single request under about 2 MB.

**Common errors**
- 401: the authorization expired or was revoked (always after 7 days while the consent screen is in *Testing*). Click **Authorize with Provider** again.
- 403 `PERMISSION_DENIED`: the account cannot open (or cannot edit) that spreadsheet, or the scope is read-only. 403 "Sheets API has not been used in project": enable the Google Sheets API in the Cloud project.
- 404: the spreadsheet id is wrong or the file was deleted.
- 400 `Unable to parse range`: the sheet name is misspelled or needs single quotes. 400 on add or rename: a sheet with that name already exists.

**Out of scope here**: finding, sharing, moving or deleting spreadsheet files (use the Google Drive connector), and Apps Script.

GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID.label: OAuth client ID
GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID.help: Google Cloud console → APIs & Services → Credentials → your OAuth client of type Web application. The same client can serve every Google connector.
GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID.patternMessage: A Google OAuth client ID ends in .apps.googleusercontent.com.

GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET.label: OAuth client secret
GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET.help: The client secret of the same OAuth client.

verifyHints.401: Google refused the access token. Click Authorize with Provider again; if the OAuth consent screen is still in Testing, set it to In production first, otherwise the authorization expires after 7 days.
verifyHints.403: The Google Sheets API is not enabled in the Google Cloud project, or the authorized scope does not allow this call. Enable it under APIs & Services → Library and authorize again.
verifyHints.rate_limited: Google Sheets is throttling this account or project (60 requests per minute per user). Wait a minute and try again.

prerequisites: A Google Cloud project with the **Google Sheets API** enabled, an OAuth consent screen (**Internal** on Google Workspace, or External set to *In production*) and a Web OAuth client with the redirect URI below. The same client can serve all Google connectors. About 10 minutes.

tools.name: gsheets_get_spreadsheet
tools.description: Get a spreadsheet's structure without cell data: title, locale, time zone, URL, and every sheet (tab) with its sheetId, title, position, hidden flag and size (rows, columns, frozen rows), plus named ranges. Call it first to learn the sheet names for ranges.

spreadsheet_id.description: Spreadsheet id, the long string in its link: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/<id>/edit.

tools.name: gsheets_read_range
tools.description: Read the cell values of one range in A1 notation (e.g. "Sheet1!A1:D50"). Returns range, majorDimension and values as a list of rows; trailing empty rows and cells are left out. Read large sheets in blocks of rows.

spreadsheet_id.description: Spreadsheet id, the long string in its link: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/<id>/edit.

range.description: Range in A1 notation, e.g. "Sheet1!A1:D20", "'Sales 2026'!A:C" (quote sheet names with spaces), "Sheet1" (the whole sheet), "A2:E" (first sheet) or a named range.

major_dimension.description: "ROWS" (default) returns a list of rows, "COLUMNS" a list of columns.

value_render_option.description: "FORMATTED_VALUE" (default, as shown in the UI), "UNFORMATTED_VALUE" (raw numbers; dates as serial numbers) or "FORMULA" (formulas instead of results).

date_time_render_option.description: With UNFORMATTED_VALUE or FORMULA: "SERIAL_NUMBER" (default) or "FORMATTED_STRING" for dates and times.

tools.name: gsheets_batch_read
tools.description: Read several ranges of one spreadsheet in a single call, e.g. ["Summary!A1:B10", "Data!A1:F100"]. Returns valueRanges, one entry per range in the same order, each with range and values.

spreadsheet_id.description: Spreadsheet id, the long string in its link: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/<id>/edit.

ranges.description: Ranges in A1 notation, e.g. ["Sheet1!A1:C10", "'Q3 data'!A:A"].

major_dimension.description: "ROWS" (default) returns a list of rows, "COLUMNS" a list of columns.

value_render_option.description: "FORMATTED_VALUE" (default, as shown in the UI), "UNFORMATTED_VALUE" (raw numbers; dates as serial numbers) or "FORMULA" (formulas instead of results).

date_time_render_option.description: With UNFORMATTED_VALUE or FORMULA: "SERIAL_NUMBER" (default) or "FORMATTED_STRING" for dates and times.

tools.name: gsheets_append_rows
tools.description: Append rows after the last row of the table found in range (e.g. "Sheet1!A:E" or just "Sheet1"), inserting new rows so nothing is overwritten. Values are parsed like typed input by default. Returns updates with updatedRange and updatedRows.

spreadsheet_id.description: Spreadsheet id, the long string in its link: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/<id>/edit.

range.description: The table to append to, e.g. "Sheet1!A:E" or "Sheet1". New rows go after its last non-empty row, starting in its first column.

items.description: A cell value: string, number, boolean or null.

values.description: Rows of cell values, e.g. [["Date", "Amount"], ["2026-10-09", 120.5]]. Each inner list is one row; use null to leave a cell unchanged and "" to empty it.

value_input_option.description: "USER_ENTERED" (default) parses values as if typed in the UI: numbers, dates, percentages and formulas starting with =. "RAW" stores them as plain text exactly as given.

tools.name: gsheets_update_range
tools.description: Write values into a range, overwriting what is there (e.g. range "Sheet1!B2:C3" with [[1, 2], [3, 4]]). Values are parsed like typed input by default, so "=SUM(A1:A9)" becomes a formula. Returns updatedRange, updatedRows and updatedCells.

spreadsheet_id.description: Spreadsheet id, the long string in its link: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/<id>/edit.

range.description: Range in A1 notation, e.g. "Sheet1!A1:D20", "'Sales 2026'!A:C" (quote sheet names with spaces), "Sheet1" (the whole sheet), "A2:E" (first sheet) or a named range.

items.description: A cell value: string, number, boolean or null.

values.description: Rows of cell values, e.g. [["Date", "Amount"], ["2026-10-09", 120.5]]. Each inner list is one row; use null to leave a cell unchanged and "" to empty it.

value_input_option.description: "USER_ENTERED" (default) parses values as if typed in the UI: numbers, dates, percentages and formulas starting with =. "RAW" stores them as plain text exactly as given.

tools.name: gsheets_batch_update_values
tools.description: Write several ranges of one spreadsheet in a single call, overwriting them: data is a list of {"range": "Sheet1!A1:B2", "values": [[...], [...]]}. Returns totalUpdatedCells and one response per range.

spreadsheet_id.description: Spreadsheet id, the long string in its link: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/<id>/edit.

items.description: A cell value: string, number, boolean or null.

value_input_option.description: "USER_ENTERED" (default) parses values as if typed in the UI: numbers, dates, percentages and formulas starting with =. "RAW" stores them as plain text exactly as given.

tools.name: gsheets_clear_range
tools.description: Empty all values in a range (formatting and validation stay), e.g. "Sheet1!A2:Z" to keep the header row. Cannot be undone through the API, only from the spreadsheet's version history. Installed switched off.

spreadsheet_id.description: Spreadsheet id, the long string in its link: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/<id>/edit.

range.description: Range in A1 notation, e.g. "Sheet1!A1:D20", "'Sales 2026'!A:C" (quote sheet names with spaces), "Sheet1" (the whole sheet), "A2:E" (first sheet) or a named range.

tools.name: gsheets_create_spreadsheet
tools.description: Create a new, empty spreadsheet in the root of the user's My Drive, with one sheet named "Sheet1" (or the locale's equivalent). Returns spreadsheetId, spreadsheetUrl and the sheets; then write with gsheets_update_range and add tabs with gsheets_add_sheet.

locale.description: Locale for formats and functions, e.g. en_US, de_DE, it_IT (default: the user's).

time_zone.description: IANA time zone for date functions, e.g. Europe/Berlin.

tools.name: gsheets_add_sheet
tools.description: Add a sheet (tab) to a spreadsheet, optionally at a position. Returns replies[0].addSheet.properties with the new sheetId and title.

spreadsheet_id.description: Spreadsheet id, the long string in its link: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/<id>/edit.

title.description: Name of the new sheet; must be unique in the spreadsheet.

tools.name: gsheets_rename_sheet
tools.description: Rename a sheet (tab). sheet_id is the numeric sheetId from gsheets_get_spreadsheet (0 for the first sheet of a new spreadsheet), not the title. Formulas that refer to the sheet are updated by Google.

spreadsheet_id.description: Spreadsheet id, the long string in its link: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/<id>/edit.

title.description: New name; must be unique in the spreadsheet.

tools.name: gsheets_batch_update
tools.description: Run Sheets API batchUpdate requests for anything the other tools do not cover: formatting (repeatCell), sorting (sortRange), inserting or deleting rows and columns (insertDimension, deleteDimension), deleting sheets (deleteSheet), freezing rows, filters, charts. Requests run in order, atomically. Installed switched off.

spreadsheet_id.description: Spreadsheet id, the long string in its link: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/<id>/edit.

requests.description: Sheets API Request objects, e.g. [{"sortRange": {"range": {"sheetId": 0, "startRowIndex": 1}, "sortSpecs": [{"dimensionIndex": 2, "sortOrder": "DESCENDING"}]}}]. Indexes are 0-based, end indexes exclusive.
